Keeps the app online when the DoH server cannot be reached, at the price of taking the poisoned answers back in exactly that moment
It only covers the DNS layer

On this device, a lookup that fails while this is on simply fails — it never drops back to plaintext DNS. Where the system already has encrypted DNS configured, the system setting is the one in force.

A hijacked or poisoned hostname connects again once DoH resolves it. But when the address itself is blocked, the handshake is cut on its SNI, or the connection is reset, no DNS helps and only a proxy will.
While a proxy is on, hostnames are resolved at the proxy and nothing here applies to those requests.
